entities.name: Quantum mechanics
entities.description: Study of matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

entities.name: Classical physics
entities.description: Physics describing matter and energy at scales familiar to human experience.

entities.name: Quantum revolution
entities.description: Shift from classical scientific models to quantum mechanics motivated by unexplained observations.

entities.name: Atomic and subatomic particles
entities.description: Small-scale physical entities studied by quantum mechanics.

entities.name: Energy quanta
entities.description: Discrete units of energy proposed to explain radiation and light-matter phenomena.

entities.name: Photon
entities.description: Quantum or smallest observable particle of the electromagnetic field.

entities.name: Electron
entities.description: Elementary particle appearing in quantum experiments and atomic models.

entities.name: Black-body radiation
entities.description: Light-intensity spectrum emitted by heated objects across frequencies.

entities.name: Photoelectric effect
entities.description: Emission of electrons from a metal when illuminated.

entities.name: Electron orbital states
entities.description: Allowed atomic electron states whose energy differences correspond to spectral lines.

entities.name: Uncertainty principle
entities.description: Principle stating that certain pairs of properties cannot be simultaneously measured or defined with arbitrary precision.

entities.name: Position
entities.description: Physical property describing location.

entities.name: Momentum
entities.description: Physical property equal to velocity multiplied by mass.

entities.name: Quantum entanglement
entities.description: Condition in which the quantum state of particles cannot be described independently, even when separated.

entities.name: Superfluidity
entities.description: Macroscopic quantum phenomenon exemplified by liquid helium flowing over a container rim.

entities.name: Wave-particle duality
entities.description: Quantum behavior in which particles and light exhibit both wave-like and particle-like characteristics.

entities.name: Wave function collapse
entities.description: Conversion of a probabilistic quantum state into a definite measured value through measurement.

entities.name: Particle spin
entities.description: Quantum degree of freedom associated with discrete magnetic properties of particles.

entities.name: Stern–Gerlach experiment
entities.description: Experiment showing a beam of silver atoms separating into two discrete streams in a magnetic field.

entities.name: Quantum field theory
entities.description: Quantum framework allowing field quantization and particle creation and annihilation.

entities.name: Quantum electrodynamics
entities.description: Quantum theory of the electromagnetic force.

entities.name: Standard Model
entities.description: Quantum field theory describing three fundamental forces and known elementary particles.

entities.name: Quantum tunneling
entities.description: Quantum process enabling electrons to penetrate a potential barrier.

entities.name: Chemistry
entities.description: Science whose atomic interactions and molecular formation can be explained using quantum mechanics.

entities.name: Molecules
entities.description: Structures formed through interactions among atoms.

entities.name: Light frequency
entities.description: Frequency of electromagnetic radiation, related in the text to photon energy.

entities.name: Electron velocity
entities.description: Velocity of electrons emitted in the photoelectric effect.

claims.statement: The correspondence principle requires quantum theory to converge to classical limits.

evidence.quote: It requires quantum theory to converge to classical limits.

claims.statement: The more precisely one property in a certain pair is measured or operationally defined, the less precisely the other can be treated.

evidence.quote: the more precisely one property is measured, or defined in operational terms, the less precisely can the other be thus treated.

claims.statement: For particles with a shared history, measuring one particle correlates with a measurement on the second even when transmission of the first result before the second measurement is impossible.

evidence.quote: This will apply even if it is impossible for the result of the first measurement to have been transmitted to the second particle before the second measurement takes place.

claims.statement: Liquid helium cooled near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over the rim of its container.

evidence.quote: if liquid helium cooled to a temperature near absolute zero is placed in a container, it spontaneously flows up and over the rim of its container

claims.statement: In the photoelectric effect, the number of emitted electrons depends on light intensity, while electron velocity does not depend on intensity.

evidence.quote: Lenard showed that the amount of current – the number of electrons – depended on the intensity of the light, but that the velocity of these electrons did not depend on intensity.

claims.statement: Einstein predicted that electron velocity increases in direct proportion to light frequency above a metal-dependent fixed value.

evidence.quote: Einstein then predicted that the electron velocity would increase in direct proportion to the light frequency above a fixed value that depended upon the metal.

claims.statement: The Stern–Gerlach experiment produced two, rather than a continuous range of, diverging streams of silver atoms.

evidence.quote: Instead, the beam separated into two, and only two, diverging streams of atoms.

claims.statement: The Standard Model does not fully explain several phenomena, including gravitation, dark matter, neutrino oscillations, and the universe's accelerating expansion.

evidence.quote: Although the Standard Model is believed to be theoretically self-consistent and has demonstrated success in providing experimental predictions, it leaves some physical phenomena unexplained and so falls short of being a complete theory of fundamental interactions.

claims.statement: Quantum tunneling is vital to a simple light switch and is used by flash memory chips to erase memory cells.

evidence.quote: Flash memory chips found in USB drives also use quantum tunneling, to erase their memory cells.

relationships.statement: Quantum mechanics is a quantum theory.

evidence.quote: The idea of quantum field theory began in the late 1920s with British physicist Paul Dirac, when he attempted to quantize the energy of the electromagnetic field; just as in quantum mechanics the energy of an electron in the hydrogen atom was quantized.

relationships.statement: The quantum revolution led to the development of quantum mechanics.

evidence.quote: The desire to resolve inconsistencies between observed phenomena and classical theory led to a revolution in physics, a shift in the original scientific paradigm: the development of quantum mechanics.

relationships.statement: Quantum mechanics helps people understand chemistry.

evidence.quote: Quantum mechanics helps people understand chemistry because it explains how atoms interact with each other and form molecules.

relationships.statement: Quantum mechanics explains how atoms interact and form molecules.

evidence.quote: it explains how atoms interact with each other and form molecules.

relationships.statement: Discrete energy quanta explain black-body radiation.

evidence.quote: Einstein's energy quanta explained the volume increase

relationships.statement: Higher light frequency increases electron velocity above a fixed metal-dependent threshold.

evidence.quote: Einstein then predicted that the electron velocity would increase in direct proportion to the light frequency above a fixed value that depended upon the metal.

relationships.statement: Measurement converts a probabilistic quantum state into a definite value through wave function collapse.

evidence.quote: Wave function collapse means that a measurement has forced or converted a quantum (probabilistic or potential) state into a definite measured value.

relationships.statement: Quantum field theory is a quantum theory extending quantum mechanics to particle creation and annihilation.

evidence.quote: QFT ... goes a step further and allows for the creation and annihilation of particles

relationships.statement: Quantum electrodynamics is a quantum field theory of electromagnetism.

evidence.quote: Quantum electrodynamics (QED) is the name of the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force.

relationships.statement: The Standard Model is a quantum field theory.

evidence.quote: The Standard Model of particle physics is the quantum field theory that describes three of the four known fundamental forces in the universe

relationships.statement: Quantum tunneling enables electrons to penetrate a potential barrier.

evidence.quote: quantum tunneling is absolutely vital, as otherwise the electrons in the electric current could not penetrate the potential barrier
